| FS-PIPELINE: Pipeline validation and finite local read execution / Enterprise / Native; owner-authorized local latest reads with collection, optional single where(condition), optional select, optional non-negative offset and optional limit | Partial, unverified | 1 / 1 | Not attested | Not attested | Not attested | Only collection / optional single where(condition) / optional select / optional non-negative offset / optional limit execute locally in that order, on the pipeline executor over rows read at one read version. Expressions are field references (nested paths included), &#95;&#95;name&#95;&#95;, literals, the six comparisons, array and map construction and document&#95;id / collection&#95;id / parent of a document reference. FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 to O-4 (production, Enterprise, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20) answered every comparison, construction, alias, select-width, literal, map-key, document-function, limit/offset and where-condition probe it was given as the official emulator does (every pair of kinds, vectors by length first and missing fields included; integers and doubles exactly as one kind; the select alias length limit of 1500 UTF-8 bytes on the unquoted joined path; argument checks of unrun stages in the recorded orders). Both profiles answer those alike. What production has not answered (a collection reference with a non-ASCII name; a key that is not a plain name in a literal holding an expression; document-function argument types other than string, integer, map and boolean; map keys other than integer and boolean; malformed or integer vectors; several empty or reserved literal keys and the key &#95;&#95;name&#95;&#95;; limit types other than integer and string, offsets other than a non-negative integer and a string; fireemu's own argument-count and option texts; an empty map or a later check after a function or stage value fireemu does not check) is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED under strict and answered as the official emulator answers it under the emulator profile. A field equality is applied by the scan without index validation (Enterprise needs no index; pending production observation). A run-time refusal may follow partial results; rows after a used-up limit are not evaluated. The same subset runs over REST :executePipeline (the Web SDK Lite transport); a REST refusal answers no partial results. Without a select a result is the whole source document (name and times); every response carries the snapshot read time as executionTime. Known differences from production: results without a sort come in another order than document names, and production puts all results of a small answer in one response or array element. Offset skips filtered rows once across the existing paged stream. All other functions/stages, logical operators and consistency selectors remain unsupported. Production execution and exact production error texts beyond the O-1 to O-4 rows remain unobserved; parser acceptance is not execution support.; execution outside collection / optional single where(condition) / optional select / optional offset / optional limit latest reads; transaction and read&#95;time execution; all functions other than the comparisons, array, map, document&#95;id, collection&#95;id and parent (including eq and between), logical operators, and all other execution stages; proxy / record-only modes; REST geo points (every REST response and write, not only pipelines): a zero coordinate is left out and a left-out coordinate reads as zero, as production answered a pipeline literal (FS-ENT-ORACLE O-3) and a document write and read (O-4), following the proto3 JSON mapping; Standard edition answers FAILED&#95;PRECONDITION FS&#95;PIPE&#95;EDITION; owner-only while rules are enforced; REST POST {database}/documents:executePipeline (the Web SDK's firestore/lite transport) on Enterprise under both profiles: the JSON ExecutePipelineRequest (structuredPipeline, transaction / newTransaction / readTime, autoCommitTransaction, requestOptions accepted and ignored; a body database must equal the URL's) runs through the same validation, compilation and executor as gRPC over one snapshot; the answer is a JSON array with one {results: &#91;document&#93;, executionTime} element per result and one {executionTime} element when there is none; refusals answer the one-element error array with the gRPC status, and a refusal answers no partial results; the strict profile's transcoder refuses unknown body fields as production's does; on Standard the strict profile answers production's FAILED&#95;PRECONDITION and the emulator profile keeps its plain 404; The finite local read subset is tested through tonic, with the Admin SDK over gRPC (firebase-admin 14.3.0 with @google-cloud/firestore 8.7.1 pipelines, tools/sdk-smoke/pipeline-admin.mjs) and over REST with the Web SDK (firebase 12.18.0 firestore/lite pipelines, tools/sdk-smoke/pipeline-lite.mjs) under both profiles. Enterprise production execution and exact production error parity beyond the FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 to O-4 rows remain unobserved. Unsupported consistency selectors, metadata expressions and execution stages are refused, never silently ignored.; known differences from FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 to O-4 (production, Enterprise, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20) within this subset: production returns results without a sort in an order that is not the document name order (fireemu returns name order), and puts all results of a small answer in one response message (gRPC) or array element (REST) where fireemu sends one result per message or element; a stored -0.0 keeps its sign in production and in fireemu under both profiles, while the official emulator stores it as 0.0 |
| FS-TEXT: Text index lifecycle and finite local lexical search / Enterprise / Native; local text catalog, explicit build controls and collection/search latest reads | Partial, unverified | 0 / unknown | Not attested | Not attested | Not attested | Local lexical-v1 analysis and approximate BM25 are not production-equivalent; productionExact refuses search until production comparison is recorded. Transactions, geo search, language morphology, enhancement and general search expression trees remain unsupported.; Production-equivalent text analysis, search scoring and error texts; fuzzy/synonym/stemming/morphological search and language autodetection; General boolean search-expression trees, geo search, query enhancement, search select, nested score aliases and non-score search sort; Search with transactions/read&#95;time, noncollection inputs, proxy execution and full Admin text-index management; Enterprise Native latest-read collection search is owner-only while Rules are configured; no new user-Rules authorization path is implied; Development defaults use a deterministic language-neutral lexical engine. Language tags/overrides are validated but enable no language-specific analysis; there is no stemming, synonym expansion, typo correction or automatic language detection; productionExact refuses every search with FS&#95;TEXT&#95;UNOBSERVED until corresponding production behavior is recorded; local tests and SDK wire compatibility do not attest production equivalence; Query bounds: 8192 UTF-8 bytes and 64 clauses. Empty or whitespace-only input, whole plain tokenless input and exclusions-only queries return no hits. Plain tokenless fragments are ignored alongside searchable terms and still count toward the clause bound; quoted or excluded tokenless fragments remain rejected. Unquoted colons delimit conjunctive terms. A leading unmatched quote leaves an ordinary conjunction, while balanced phrases remain positional within one field. OR/or is conjunctive between positive operands and searchable alone; other OR contexts remain unsupported. Legacy field-qualified quoted phrases remain unobserved development approximations, not native-compatible qualified phrase support. Only string-valued indexed fields produce postings. Real posting data is reconstructed at the query snapshot; this is not an incremental-commit performance claim; Local build controls are explicit; a supplied generation fences stale operations. Catalog source/progress/postings are isolated and participate in session snapshot/reset ownership and retained-byte estimates; Standard edition still accepts valid searchConfig files without serving search. Geo-only definitions remain outside the text catalog. Search definitions never satisfy an ordinary composite-index requirement |
